title: Thumbelina
summary: A tiny girl named Thumbelina embarks on a brave adventure after a toad captures her.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a good woman wanted a child very much, but she did not know how to get one.
She went to see a wise old woman who gave her a little grain to plant.
After the grain grew into a large, beautiful flower, it opened up to reveal a tiny girl inside.
Because she was no bigger than a finger, the woman called her a special name.
She was so small that people could hardly see her without care.
The little girl had a nice bed made from a shell and spent her days singing sweet songs.
One night, an ugly animal jumped through the window and carried the little girl away into the garden.
The creature wanted the girl to marry her son.
So she left the poor child alone on a green plant in the water.
The child began to cry because she did not want to live with the ugly family.
Some fish in the water felt very sorry for her and helped pull the plant away from the land.
Then a large fly came down, caught the girl, and carried her high up into a tree.
However, the other animals did not like how she looked, so the first left her alone in the forest.
The little girl lived through the warm summer by herself, eating sweet food from flowers and drinking water from plants.
She tried to find happiness while the sun shone upon her face every single day.
Many hours passed as she sang songs to the trees and the sky.
When cold winter came, the weather grew very bad, and the girl had to walk through the snow.
She found a small home under a tree where a kind field animal lived.
The creature gave her food and a warm bed, but soon told her that a rich neighbor wanted to marry her.
The girl did not like the rich neighbor because he lived down below the earth and never saw the sun.
She tried to think of a way to escape from that dark place.
During her stay there, she found a bird that seemed dead upon the cold ground.
The girl took care of the bird and brought it back to life with her love.
When spring came again, the bird wanted to fly away to a warm country and asked the girl to go with him.
The girl climbed upon the bird, and they flew far away across the sea.
They traveled together for many days until they reached a wonderful land.
The bird brought her to a wonderful land full of lovely flowers and green trees.
There, a tiny king lived inside the most beautiful flower in the garden.
When he saw the girl, he fell in love with her and asked her to marry him.
She finally found her true home, and they lived happily together forever after.
The sun shone brightly upon their wedding day as all the flowers danced in the wind.

They spent their days walking among the lovely plants and talking about their future.
Nothing could ever trouble their calm life in that wonderful land.
The fish in the distant river sometimes swam close to the garden to see if she was well.
The bird often returned to visit them and share stories from distant countries.
The good woman who wanted a child was remembered with love in the heart of the girl.
Every single moment was filled with joy, peace, and quiet happiness.
The wind whispered softly through the leaves of the tall trees.
The bright colors of the flowers made the entire place look like a dream.
The little girl knew that she would never feel sad again.
Her heart was full of thankfulness for all the friends who helped her along the way.
Thus, the story of the tiny girl reached its perfect and happy end.

sentences.text: Long ago, a woman possessed an aching desire for a child of her own, yet she remained utterly at a loss regarding how to attain such a blessing.
Seeking counsel from a wise old woman who dwelt nearby, she received a tiny, peculiar grain of barley.
Planted within a modest flowerpot, the seed swiftly germinated into a magnificent tulip with velvety red and yellow petals.
When the blossom finally unfurled its tightly bound layers, the woman gasped to discover a living infant girl sitting squarely at its center.
Because her stature did not exceed that of a single human thumb, the astonished mother bestowed upon her the name Thumbelina.
So diminutive was the child that a polished walnut shell served as her cradle, while violet petals functioned as soft blankets.
Throughout the daylight hours, she amused herself by singing delicate melodies that resonated softly against the walls of the humble cottage.
Her tranquility was shattered one evening when an atrocious toad, slimy and large, leaped clumsily through the shattered glass of the window.
Snatching the walnut shell while Thumbelina slept, the creature hopped back out into the garden and deposited the frightened girl upon a broad lily pad.
The toad intended for the captive maiden to wed her hideous son, leaving the weeping child stranded amidst the dark, stagnant water.
Staring into the murky depths below, Thumbelina felt a crushing wave of despair as she contemplated a lifetime bound to the repulsive family.
Fortunately, a school of silvery fish swimming beneath the surface noticed her plight and immediately took pity on the distressed prisoner.
Nibbling diligently at the thick green stem, they managed to sever it from the muddy bottom, allowing the lily pad to drift far away from the shore.
Before she could draw a breath of relief, a magnificent cockchafer beetle swooped down from the canopy with a loud buzz.
Clutching her tightly in his wiry legs, the insect carried her high into the branches of a towering oak tree, far above the meadows.
High among the sunlit leaves, the beetle presented his captive to his aristocratic friends, expecting them to shower her with praise.
Instead, the other insects wrinkled their delicate antennae in disgust, declaring that the strange creature with only two legs was utterly hideous.
Even the beetle quickly altered his opinion, abandoning the lonely girl upon a mossy branch and flying away without a backward glance.
For the remainder of the warm summer months, Thumbelina survived entirely on her own ingenuity and the bounty of the forest.
She dined upon the sweet nectar hidden inside wild blossoms and quenched her thirst with morning dew collected carefully from broad green leaves.
Hours melted into lazy afternoons as she sang solitary songs to the indifferent clouds and the overarching branches of the ancient trees.
When autumn yielded to the bitter breath of winter, however, the landscape transformed into a desolate expanse of blinding white snow.
Shivering violently in her thin summer dress, the little wanderer trudged through the drifts until she stumbled upon a small burrow beneath the roots of a cornstalk.
Inside lived a generous field mouse who took pity on the frozen visitor and offered her a warm refuge from the howling winds.
Thumbelina repaid this kindness by performing daily chores and reciting lovely stories to entertain her gracious host during the long evenings.
Peace reigned within the subterranean dwelling until the field mouse proudly introduced her wealthy neighbor, a blind mole draped in a luxurious velvet coat.
Although the mole possessed vast underground riches and a remarkably spacious estate, he harbored a profound aversion to the sun and the open sky.
Impressed by Thumbelina's sweet voice, the wealthy gentleman resolved to make her his bride, dismissing her protests with quiet indifference.
He expected the grateful girl to spend her entire existence in his dark, damp tunnels, far removed from the warmth of daylight.
Trapped in such narrow circumstances, Thumbelina dreaded the impending marriage and secretly wept whenever she ventured down the dreary corridors.
During her exploration of a long, abandoned tunnel that connected the mole's estate to the surface, she stumbled upon a motionless swallow.
The bird lay stretched out upon the cold earth with its wings pinned rigidly to its sides, apparently frozen to death by the harsh winter.
Kneeling beside the fragile creature, Thumbelina felt a sudden surge of compassion and pressed her ear against its feathered chest.
Though the heartbeat was terribly faint, she detected a lingering spark of life and resolved to nurse the unfortunate animal back to health.
She wove a thick blanket of soft grass to keep the swallow warm and carried tiny morsels of food to its beak every single day.
Spring finally returned with gentle rains and warm breezes that melted the stubborn snow and awakened the dormant earth.
Restored to full strength, the grateful swallow fluttered its wings and announced its intention to fly away to a sun-drenched southern land.
Inviting Thumbelina to accompany him upon his back, the bird offered her a miraculous escape from the impending wedding underground.
Hesitating only for a fleeting moment, the girl climbed eagerly onto the feathered shoulders and bade farewell to the dark tunnels forever.
They soared gracefully across shimmering blue seas for many days, watching mountains and forests shrink into miniature paintings below them.
At last, the swallow descended toward a breathtaking valley where white marble pillars gleamed amidst an ocean of fragrant blossoms.
He carried his passenger directly to the capital of this floral paradise, depositing her gently upon the petal of a magnificent white flower.
To her utter astonishment, a tiny king with a crown of spun gold and translucent wings sat enthroned at the very heart of the blossom.
The miniature monarch was captivated by Thumbelina's radiant smile and immediately asked if she would consent to become his queen.
Realizing she had finally discovered a place where she truly belonged, the joyful bride accepted the proposal without hesitation.
From that day onward, Thumbelina lived in absolute harmony with her royal husband, surrounded by beauty and eternal spring.
Every morning, the sun rose majestically above the green canopy, warming the earth and encouraging the flowers to open wide.
The tiny king listened with boundless devotion as his beloved wife filled the palace gardens with her enchanting morning songs.
Nothing ever threatened their peaceful existence in that wonderful land, and even the friendly fish occasionally swam up the river to check on her.
The swallow frequently returned from distant journeys to share wondrous tales of the outside world before resting in the branches above.
Remembrance of the kind field mouse and the good woman who first desired a child remained forever cherished in the young queen's heart.
No shadow of sorrow ever touched her spirit again, for she knew that true friendship and love could conquer any trial.
The gentle wind whispered softly through the leaves, carrying the sweet scent of blossoms across the entire valley.
Every single moment was filled with profound gratitude as the little girl reflected upon her long and winding journey.
Thus, the remarkable tale of Thumbelina reached its joyous conclusion, sealed by the bright light of a sunlit wedding day.
